But I said, “You’re using American-made steel.” So I’m trying to get that out of him: how much he’s paying for steel.Obviously, he’s not going to tell me, but he does say, “We have a strategic long-term relationship with our supplier.” That tells you a lot, which is that there are ways you can do these things. You have to work with your suppliers. You have to give them longer-term arrangements, be less transactional, more strategic on things like that. So I think you can do it, but it really takes a comprehensive and more thoughtful approach.I understand the rationale for putting tariffs on foreign goods that undercut our markets. You’re just going to increase the cost, and then maybe the consumer will buy the domestic product, and that’s better for our economy. It just hasn’t seemed to have worked.I don’t see Liberation Day as having done anything except generally raise prices on everything. We haven’t actually remapped the global economy. And a lot of what you’re describing is, well, the system is pretty resilient. The system was pretty resilient to COVID. The system was pretty resilient to an oil tanker getting stuck in the Suez Canal. The system has been pretty resilient to the war in Iran. The system has been pretty resilient to absolutely chaotic tariffs.Maybe some prices have risen, and I’m sure we’re going to get listeners pointing out that all the prices have risen. It feels like the only thing the system isn’t resilient to is the AI industry wanting every scrap of RAM that the whole world can produce. And so now there’s not going to be inexpensive cell phones.What will push the system over the breaking point? Because globalization has seemed generally resilient to a bunch of people who want it to be over.I think what you’re highlighting is that it’s really the power of the market. In the case of closing the Strait of Hormuz, Brent North Sea crude prices didn’t go to $150 a barrel like I was afraid they would, and a lot of people were afraid they would because the market adjusted.We applied a lot of tariffs on Liberation Day. The first response was circumvention or front-running. The next response was tariff engineering. The next response is like, “Okay, let me move production to Vietnam or let me move production to Mexico, and I’ll find a way around that.” Now, eventually, when you close down all those things, then prices eventually have to rise.In the case of memory chips, that’s a different problem because the demand far outstripped the capacity. I used to always buy memory cards on Black Friday. Forget that this year.Yeah, it’s all over.I’m just glad I stocked up on a previous Black Friday.If you want to know my prediction for when the AI industry will meet its true political end, it’s when Grand Theft Auto VI comes out. Everyone goes out to buy a PS5, and they realize it’s more expensive now at the end of its life cycle than it was at the beginning because the price of memory has skyrocketed.Yeah, no kidding. We’re talking about huge amounts. But that’s the same thing. We’re in a phase where we see all these tactical actions taken by the government, very transactional, without necessarily understanding all the complex interconnections and interdependencies.You may have noticed, for example, that the administration temporarily suspended the Jones Act. I don’t know if you remember that. Why did they temporarily suspend the Jones Act? Because oil refineries on the East Coast of the US couldn’t get their oil from Texas cheaply because there were no domestic supertankers.The Jones Act requires that if you move stuff from Texas to New Jersey, you have to have a US-owned, US-crewed, US-built, very large crude carrier. There aren’t any because we don’t build those in the US. So that’s why it’s cheaper to bring oil from Algeria to New Jersey than it is to bring it from Texas. And that’s why they suspended the Jones Act for a while. At least they understood that.I know at least some of our audience is going to be listening to this conversation, and you’re steeped in global trade. You wrote a book to educate our government about how it works from the basics, which I think is sorely needed.But a lot of the promise for young people in our politics lately is that we will rebuild American capacity. We will rebuild manufacturing capacity. We will bring back a bunch of jobs where you don’t need an advanced degree in AI prompt engineering or whatever to see the future. We will bring back the dignity of work.Politicians on both sides are making these promises all the time, and a lot of that requires closing down trade, forcing that economic activity back within our borders. It just seems like that isn’t likely. So I’m not going to ask you whether or not that is totally likely. I’m going to ask: what’s more likely instead?Well, I think what’s more likely is that we will see efforts as you describe. I would love to sit down with people and say, okay, we want to move this type of production back to the US. Let’s take a more strategic, more nuanced approach, understanding the bigger picture, considering what levers are available.The US is still a big, attractive market. It is the largest market in the world. It is the most attractive market in the world. That’s, by the way, why the Chinese all want to come here: because they can make some money here that they can’t make elsewhere. So then how do we harness that market power and that market pull with a more nuanced understanding of why our supply chains are organized the way they are today? Recognizing that, can I build a strategy to bring important things that are very strategic for the US to know how to do?Let’s think about how we fix this problem with an understanding of that bigger picture.Willy, it’s been great to talk to you. It is always just a pleasure. We have to have you back faster than five years. Thank you so much for being on Decoder.Thanks for having me.Questions or comments? Hit us up at decoder@theverge.com. We really do read every email!Decoder with Nilay PatelA podcast from The Verge about big ideas and other problems.SUBSCRIBE NOW!
history.author: Nilay Patel
history.titleZh: AI热潮背后隐藏的供应链成本
history.descriptionZh:
这是一场围绕全球供应链未来走向的深度访谈。主持人Nilay Patel与哈佛商学院管理实践教授、经济学家Willy Shih展开对话，后者刚刚出版新书《我的东西从哪来？全球供应链背后的强大经济学》。访谈背景设定在一个全球化遭遇多重压力的时刻：特朗普政府关税政策反复变动、制造业回流承诺大多落空、AI基础设施竞赛吞噬全球计算资源，而政界关于"全球化是否正在终结"的争论愈演愈烈。Shih的核心论点是：全球供应链的形态归根结底由经济学力量驱动，政治意志若无视这一底层逻辑，其政策目标往往会被市场以各种方式规避或扭曲。

Shih首先回顾了他准确预判富士康威斯康星州LCD工厂项目失败的经历。他从第一性原理出发，指出当地缺乏支撑面板工厂所需的玻璃基板供应商和足够的结构钢材与混凝土用量，而面板制造对厂房稳定性有极高要求。这一案例成为他分析供应链问题的典型方法：不只看组装环节，而要追溯整个配套生态。

关于全球化的基本原理，Shih强调劳动力套利和专业化分工是贸易的根本驱动力。他以冷冻鱼从阿拉斯加运到中国青岛加工再运回、腰果在越南加工等看似反常的贸易路线为例，说明这些都是成本最优的经济选择。当美国对中国商品加征关税后，市场的第一反应是规避——2025年第一季度美国从爱尔兰进口创历史纪录，随后半年进口骤降，正是企业提前囤货的结果；同时，中国至墨西哥之间新开通多条直达海运集装箱航线，实质是将零部件运至墨西哥组装，再以《美墨加协定》框架免税进入美国市场，直接绕开关税壁垒。

在贸易失衡问题上，Shih指出中国持续运行巨额贸易顺差，实际上是将自身经济问题出口到美国，以牺牲他国就业为代价。欧洲尤其是德国已开始意识到汽车产业面临的生存危机。他认为，理想的解决方案是构建一个以北美为核心、联合欧洲、日本、东南亚、澳大利亚、新西兰及部分中南美洲和非洲国家的"志同道合贸易集团"，在集团内实现专业化分工，同时确保关键矿产、低成本劳动力和技术专长的可获得性，这比单打独斗策略更优。

访谈深入对比了中美制造业生态。Shih指出，中国制造业优势并非简单来自"窃取"技术，更多是"学习"——苹果和特斯拉等企业为满足自身严苛的规格、性能和成本要求，实际上倒逼中国供应商大幅提升了制造能力。他特别强调三个被忽视的维度：其一，中国从五年规划到1986年"863计划"的长远规划能力，虽早期犯过重大错误，但持续从错误中学习，规划质量显著提升；其二，中国地方政府之间形成激烈竞争格局，各省市相互比拼产业目标，制造出类似自由市场的残酷竞争动态；其三，中国负责产业规划的经济官员多为机械、电气、冶金等工科背景，而美国华盛顿的相关官员多出身政治学、经济学和法学，缺乏对制造流程的实际认知。此外，中国工厂在自动化投资上极为激进，两三年即淘汰设备升级换代，以"更多资本开支"应对一切竞争威胁。

以iPhone为例，Shih展示了全球最复杂消费品的供应链全貌：最先进的芯片来自台积电台湾厂（亚利桑那工厂产能与之相比微不足道），制造芯片所需的高端设备来自荷兰ASML以及美国Lam Research和Applied Materials；钛金属从宾夕法尼亚州Perryman公司采购后运往中国，最终整机在中国完成组装。组装环节仍需大量人工，中国通过继承自革命时期的"单位"模式，能够动员十万至二十万工人在封闭园区内实现规模化手工装配，印度正在尝试复制但难度极大。Shih认为iPhone是理解供应链问题难度的绝佳样本：它同时依赖最高端技术和最庞大的劳动力动员能力。

关于制造业回流，Shih直言美国是高成本国家，回流的制造业岗位必须具备高劳动生产率或高度差异化。他以喷气发动机热端高温合金为例，全球仅三家公司掌握铸造技术，两家在美国、一家在英国，这类高壁垒产品才是美国制造业的合理定位。他批评当前关税政策的交易性和不稳定性：2025至2026年间关税行动散布如"霰弹枪打墙"，企业无法做出十年至二十年回收期的长期投资决策，半导体厂和汽车厂选址尤为受制。汽车行业原本的全球分工策略——宝马在南卡罗来纳生产X系列出口全球、同时进口其他系列——也被关税打乱。他提到"鸡肉税"的历史案例，说明对轻型卡车的关税扭曲了底特律车企的产品结构，使其长期依赖高利润SUV和皮卡，消费者为此支付更高价格。

在系统韧性方面，Shih认为市场调整能力极强：霍尔木兹海峡危机未使布伦特原油飙升至每桶150美元，苏伊士运河堵塞和新冠冲击均被消化。但当前真正的稀缺瓶颈是AI产业对内存芯片的吞噬性需求，叠加关税层层收紧后价格终将上行。主持人调侃称，等到《侠盗猎车手VI》发售时玩家发现PS5因内存涨价而更贵，可能就是AI产业触及政治临界点的时刻。Shih还提到政府曾临时暂停《琼斯法案》以缓解东海岸炼油厂无法廉价获取德州原油的问题，恰恰说明决策者偶尔也能理解供应链互联性。

最后，Shih呼吁采取更具战略性和精细化的产业政策：美国仍是全球最大、最具吸引力的市场，这正是中国企业希望进入的原因；应利用这一市场引力，在理解供应链现有结构的基础上，有针对性地将真正具有战略意义的能力留在或引回国内，而非依赖粗糙的关税工具。他指出，政治人物关于恢复制造业尊严和就业的承诺需要更细致的产业理解来支撑，否则政策效果可能适得其反。

history.title: You can post AI music straight to SoundCloud from ElevenLabs
history.description:
BERLIN, GERMANY - JANUARY 16: In this photo illustration the logo of the music streaming service SoundCloud is displayed on a smartphone on January 16, 2019 in Berlin, Germany. (Photo by Thomas Trutschel/Photothek via Getty Images) | Photothek via Getty Images	

After partnering with Moises earlier this year, SoundCloud is now adding integration with another AI music platform, ElevenLabs. history.content: After partnering with Moises earlier this year, SoundCloud is now adding integration with another AI music platform, ElevenLabs. Now, rather than having to export and download your outputs from ElevenLabs and then upload them to SoundCloud, you can publish them directly. As part of the partnership, SoundCloud Artist Pro subscribers are also getting three months of ElevenMusic Pro for free, so they can experiment with generative AI and potentially alienate their fans. Songs published from ElevenLabs directly to SoundCloud will be labeled as such, making clear their AI origins.The integration between SoundCloud and ElevenLabs isn’t as deep as the Moises integration. That lets users pull tracks from SoundCloud into Moises for stem separation and remixing, then republish them directly to SoundCloud.In general, SoundCloud has seemed more willing to embrace AI-generated music than other streaming services. While it “encourages” users subject to EU rules to label tracks as “AI-generated or manipulated” and has rules against impersonation, it’s also partnered with multiple generative AI music platforms. SoundCloud has also avoided the loud-and-proud press releases detailing how many spammy AI songs it’s removed from its platform, or bragging about demonetizing them.
history.author: Terrence O’Brien
history.titleZh: 你可以直接从 ElevenLabs 将 AI 音乐发布到 SoundCloud
history.descriptionZh:
SoundCloud 正在扩大对 AI 生成音乐的支持。继今年早些时候与 AI 音乐平台 Moises 合作后，SoundCloud 又与另一家 AI 音乐平台 ElevenLabs 达成集成。此前，用户需要先从 ElevenLabs 导出并下载生成结果，再上传到 SoundCloud；现在，用户可以将 ElevenLabs 的输出直接发布到 SoundCloud。作为合作的一部分，SoundCloud Artist Pro 订阅用户还可免费获得三个月 ElevenMusic Pro，用于试验生成式 AI 音乐创作，尽管这也可能让部分粉丝感到不适。凡是从 ElevenLabs 直接发布到 SoundCloud 的歌曲都会被明确标注，以说明其 AI 来源。

从技术集成深度看，SoundCloud 与 ElevenLabs 的合作不如与 Moises 的集成深入。Moises 集成允许用户将 SoundCloud 上的曲目拉入 Moises，进行分轨分离和混音，然后再直接重新发布回 SoundCloud；而与 ElevenLabs 的集成目前主要解决的是 AI 生成音乐从创作平台到分发平台的一键发布问题，减少导出、下载、上传等中间环节。新闻未披露具体的性能参数或量化对比数据，核心差异体现在工作流简化程度和平台间集成深度上。

整体来看，SoundCloud 相比其他流媒体服务更愿意接纳 AI 生成音乐。平台一方面“鼓励”受欧盟规则约束的用户将曲目标注为“AI 生成或被操纵”，并制定了禁止冒充他人的规则；另一方面已与多个生成式 AI 音乐平台建立合作。与一些高调宣传删除垃圾 AI 歌曲或取消其变现资格的平台不同，SoundCloud 并未大张旗鼓地发布此类治理数据。此次集成的影响在于：AI 音乐创作者可以更便捷地在 SoundCloud 发布和实验作品，平台通过来源标注提升透明度，但 AI 音乐大量涌入也可能带来内容质量、粉丝接受度和平台治理方面的挑战。应用场景主要覆盖 AI 音乐创作、生成式音乐实验、分轨混音再发布以及订阅捆绑试用等。

history.title: Intel leaker claims Nova Lake desktop chips have 5.1 GHz clock limit beyond 90°C
history.description: A known Intel leaker claims that Intel's next-generation processors will top out at 5.1 GHz if the CPU core temperatures aren't kept below 90°C.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 7 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter According to new information from reasonably reliable Intel leaker Jaykihn, Intel's upcoming Nova Lake desktop CPUs will have an unusual limiter applied. He claims that the next-gen desktop parts from Intel will "universally limit the maximum core frequency to 5.1 GHz when above 90°C." That doesn't mean the parts will top out at 5.1 GHz, which would be disastrous, but it does mean that you're going to need some darn good cooling to reach high clock rates on Nova Lake desktop CPUs.Go deeper with TH Premium: CPU (Image credit: Tom's Hardware)Intel VP Robert Hallock sets Nova Lake expectations, teases return to Raptor Lake for DDR4 platformsCPU scaling with DLSSIntel's one-two punch plan in desktop CPUs is taking shapeBenchmarking AMD's BC-250, offering Steam Machine-like performance at half the priceAMD splits Zen 7 into three EPYC families for 2028 and starts selling server CPUs by the agent Let's be clear about what he's saying. He's not saying that Nova Lake CPUs can't go above 5.1 GHz. He's also not saying that Nova Lake CPUs have their thermal limit at 90°C. While Jaykihn doesn't provide any clock rate information, he does imply that the chips will go above that, possibly quite significantly, as long as the thermals are kept in check, and he does say that the "Tjmax" value of Nova Lake is 100°C. Notably, that's a drop from 105°C in Arrow Lake, although prior-gen Raptor Lake CPUs had the same 100°C peak.Preliminary. Nova Lake -S desktop processors will universally limit the maximum core frequency to 5.1GHz when above 90C. This is separate behavior from traditional TJMax thermal throttling at 100C. Alike TJMax, this temperature threshold cannot be shifted upwards.November 4, 2026The mechanism that this most clearly resembles is Intel's own Thermal Velocity Boost. TVB, if you're not familiar, is the feature that allows high-end Intel CPUs to hit their highest clock rates. Put simply, TVB simply says that if the chip isn't overheating, it can go 100-300 MHz higher than its rated Turbo Boost Max speed. It's a little confusing, because these TVB clock rates are often quoted as the "Max Turbo Frequency"; Intel even does this itself. But TVB clocks are not the same as standard turbo clocks, and a lot of users who don't have exotic cooling probably never actually see these speeds in practice since they do require optimal conditions.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Does this mean that the practical limit of Nova Lake desktop CPU clocks is 5.1 GHz? Well, that depends on how hard these parts are to cool. Remember, we're dealing with chips fabricated on a 2nm-class process; in this case, it's reportedly TSMC's N2P for the compute tiles, while the peripheral chiplets are all on Intel's own 18A or 18A-P. This has consequences, as N2P is reportedly much denser than 18A, but it also lacks back-side power delivery, which means that the thermal resistance of the individual dies is considerably lower. Combined with much lower power consumption from a real node step, it may turn out that Nova Lake is actually quite easy to keep cool.Ultimately, that is going to depend in part on how much Intel decides to push the "fMax", or maximum frequency. Rumors have put AMD's Zen 6 desktop Ryzen processors above 6 GHz for peak clock rates; if that's true, Intel could be looking at as much as a 20% clock rate disadvantage at 5.1 GHz. Obviously, as noted above, the chips are expected to have a higher fMax than that, but it remains to be seen how easily users can keep the parts cool enough to make use of the extra clock rate headroom given this new limit. Both Intel's flagship Core Ultra 9 285K and the Red Team's extant Zen 5-based Ryzen 9 9950X can reach 5.7 GHz before overclocking. You may like Leaked Intel Nova Lake product list has three 'BFC' chips with up to 144MB of game-boosting L3 cache Intel's Core Ultra 400 'Nova Lake' launch schedule leaks out Intel confirms Nova Lake CPUs will use advanced 18A-P node, more details at CES Intel's familiar eXtreme Tuning Utility (XTU) software gives users full control over TVB, Tjmax, and core turbo ratios. (Image credit: Future)For tuners, a frustrating detail is that this 5.1 GHz hard clock limit apparently "cannot be raised." That means folks doing system tuning on Nova Lake will be strongly encouraged to undervolt to reduce the thermal output of their processors and help them maintain high performance. That's unusual, as historically Intel allows users to adjust the thermal throttle point of their processors when overclocking. That may potentially still be the case on processors unlocked for overclocking, of course; Jaykihn is reporting based on leaks and engineering samples rather than final released products.Even if Nova Lake doesn't scale clocks much over Arrow Lake, it could still be quite a bit faster than the previous generation. Recall that the new chips will come with new core architectures and new technologies, including APX core extensions and bLLC, Intel's long-awaited response to AMD's 3D V-Cache. Forecasts are indicating that gaming performance could be as much as 33% faster than Arrow Lake, which would be huge. However, this 5.1 GHz limit could be a downer for people who are interested in the rumored 52-core version of Nova Lake. We'll find out how much it matters when the Core Ultra 4000 series launches either very late this year or very early next year, although we wouldn't expect the 52-core flagship or bLLC versions until next summer.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.
history.author: Zak Killian
history.titleZh: 英特尔爆料人称Nova Lake桌面芯片在超过90°C时时钟频率限制为5.1 GHz
history.descriptionZh:
据Tom's Hardware报道，可信度较高的Intel爆料者Jaykihn称，Intel下一代桌面CPU Nova Lake将引入一项不寻常的频率限制：当温度超过90°C时，最大核心频率会被统一限制在5.1GHz。关键点在于，这并不意味着Nova Lake最高只能运行5.1GHz，而是高温状态下无法继续维持更高频率；只要散热足够好，芯片预计仍可超过5.1GHz，具体最高频率尚未披露。该机制独立于传统的Tjmax热节流：Nova Lake的Tjmax为100°C，低于Arrow Lake的105°C，与Raptor Lake相同；据报道，90°C阈值和5.1GHz硬限制均不能向上调整。这一行为类似Intel的Thermal Velocity Boost：TVB允许CPU在温度允许时比额定Turbo Boost Max再高100-300MHz，常被宣传为“Max Turbo Frequency”，但需要理想散热才能实际达到。因此，Nova Lake高频率的实际可用性将高度依赖散热条件。

工艺和热设计方面，Nova Lake据称采用2nm级工艺：计算Tile由台积电N2P制造，外围chiplet则使用Intel 18A或18A-P。N2P密度高于18A，但缺少背面供电，原文称这会令单个裸片的热阻显著更低；叠加真实制程步进带来的功耗下降，Nova Lake可能并不难冷却。不过，能否充分利用5.1GHz以上的频率余量，仍取决于Intel设定的fMax。对比来看，当前旗舰Core Ultra 9 285K和Ryzen 9 9950X在未超频时均可达到5.7GHz；传闻AMD Zen 6桌面Ryzen峰值将超过6GHz。若Nova Lake实际可用频率停留在5.1GHz，可能面临最高约20%的频率劣势，但预期其fMax会高于5.1GHz，实际差距取决于散热和最终调校。

对调优用户而言，90°C以上锁5.1GHz且该硬限制不能提高，意味着需要更积极降压以降低发热、维持高性能；这与Intel历史上允许超频用户调整热节流点的做法不同。不过Jaykihn的信息基于泄漏和工程样品，最终零售版及解锁超频型号是否保留可调空间仍待确认。即便频率提升受限，Nova Lake仍将带来新核心架构、APX扩展和bLLC——Intel对标AMD 3D V-Cache的大缓存技术，有预测称其游戏性能可比Arrow Lake快最多33%。该限制可能对传闻中的52核旗舰影响更大。Core Ultra 4000系列预计今年底或明年初发布，52核旗舰及bLLC版本可能要到明年夏天。总体看，Nova Lake的性能释放将更依赖散热，90°C/5.1GHz限制是重要变量。

history.title: ‘Hogwarts Legacy’ Gets a Magical NVIDIA DLSS 5 Upgrade on GeForce NOW
history.description: Hogwarts Legacy receives an NVIDIA DLSS 5 upgrade with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering today, bringing lifelike lighting and materials to the wizarding world on GeForce NOW. Blizzard Entertainment’s World of Warcraft: Forever also opens a new chapter in Azeroth, with a launch-week access reward available for GeForce NOW members. Meanwhile, Ubisoft brings fresh challenges with expansions […]
history.content: Hogwarts Legacy receives an NVIDIA DLSS 5 upgrade with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering today, bringing lifelike lighting and materials to the wizarding world on GeForce NOW. Blizzard Entertainment’s World of Warcraft: Forever also opens a new chapter in Azeroth, with a launch-week access reward available for GeForce NOW members. Meanwhile, Ubisoft brings fresh challenges with expansions for Tom Clancy’s The Division 2 and Anno 117: Pax Romana. It’s all part of a packed month of play, with two-dozen games joining the GeForce NOW library throughout November, including eight this week. Hogwarts in a New Light NVIDIA DLSS 5 with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering arrives in Hogwarts Legacy today, giving members a new reason to return to Hogwarts, streaming from Steam, Epic Games and Xbox with Play Anywhere support. Published by Warner Bros. Games under the Portkey Games label and developed by Avalanche Software, Hogwarts Legacy is an immersive, open-world action role-playing game set in the 1800s wizarding world. Begin as a fifth-year student, encounter magical creatures, brew potions and learn spells while exploring both recognizable and unfamiliar places. The update adds lifelike lighting and material detail while retaining underlying geometry and textures. Avalanche Software has tuned the integration through DLSS 5’s developer controls to maintain the game’s artistic intent and style. Hogwarts Legacy also includes support for the DLSS Multi Frame Generation and Ray Reconstruction features, accelerating and enhancing the ray-traced graphics that immerse players in Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry. Thanks to NVIDIA DLSS 4.5 controls in the cloud, members can fine-tune their experience. Ultimate members can experience the update with GeForce RTX 5080-class performance across PCs, Macs, handhelds, browsers, mobile devices, compatible TVs and more, without an expensive PC upgrade or waiting for game downloads. GeForce NOW handles the installs and updates, saving the storage space for everyday essentials. Just pick up the wand, hop on a broom and take flight. A New Chapter, Forever Familiar roads. New discoveries. Blizzard Entertainment’s World of Warcraft: Forever launched Wednesday, Nov. 4, and is streaming on GeForce NOW, inviting players into a reimagined original Azeroth built to keep growing for years to come. Explore new and expanded zones, discover gameplay enhancements and take in upgraded graphics in a world where community and the journey take center stage. Access is included with an active World of Warcraft subscription or Game Time, giving returning heroes and newcomers a fresh starting point. GeForce NOW also supports CurseForge Addons for World of Warcraft: Forever, giving premium members more ways to customize their experience. At launch, GeForce NOW plans to support around 100 of the most popular CurseForge add-ons, with the selection evolving to reflect player favorites. Members can request additional add-ons through in-app feedback for consideration in future updates. The cloud keeps the next quest within reach across supported devices. For new World of Warcraft users who don’t already have a subscription, a launch-week access reward is available across all GeForce NOW membership tiers. The access period runs through Wednesday, Nov. 11, at 11:59 p.m. PT. Eligible members can sign in to their GeForce NOW account and head to the Account Portal to redeem while supplies last, on a first-come, first-served basis. Gather the party and venture forward. New Missions, New Horizons From city streets to Roman roads. Ubisoft brings two new downloadable content releases to the cloud this week, sending agents into an overgrown New York and governors toward a new province of the Roman Empire. Launched earlier this week, Tom Clancy’s The Division 2: Echoes of Central Park is the biggest experience since Tom Clancy’s The Division 2: Warlords of New York, opening up Central Park and the Upper West Side for the first time in franchise history. Investigate disappearances and rumors of a mysterious threat, team up with three companions with distinct combat roles, and earn new gear and six skill variants. Play solo or in co-op, with a level boost available for agents below level 40. In Anno 117: Pax Romana – Dawn of the Delta, arriving today, build cities in Aegyptus, where deserts, fertile farmland and seasonal floods shape every decision. Develop irrigation systems and choose whether to Romanize the population or preserve local traditions. The new province can be explored in an existing save or chosen as the starting point for a new game. New territory belongs on the map, not in a download queue. GeForce NOW handles both expansions’ downloads and updates, leaving the planning to governors and the gear management to agents. In addition, members can look for the following joining the GeForce NOW library this week: World of Warcraft: Forever (New release on Battle.net, Nov. 4) County of Fortune (New release on Steam, Nov. 5) CURE – A Hospital Simulator (Steam) Leaf it Alone (Steam) Planet Zoo 2 (Epic Games Store) Probably Stolen – Cyberpunk Shopkeeper Sim (Steam) RuneScape: Dragonwilds (Epic Games Store) SpiritVale (Steam) And the November lineup has more in store. Look forward to these games arriving throughout the rest of the month: Ashes of the Singularity II (New release on Steam, Nov. 10) Cyberpunk 2077 (New release on Battle.net, Nov. 10, and Xbox, supports Xbox Play Anywhere) Warhammer Survivors (New release on Steam and Xbox, available on Game Pass, Nov. 10) Main Sequence (New release on Steam, Nov. 12) Volvy’s Adventure: Reslimed (New release on Steam, Nov. 19) Appulse (New release on Steam, Nov. 26) Baldur’s Gate 3 (Xbox, supports Xbox Play Anywhere) Deadly Days: Roadtrip (Steam) Gone Fishing (Steam) Graveyard Keeper (Steam) Graveyard Keeper 2 (Epic Games Store and GOG) Quasimorph (Steam) Tape to Tape (Steam) The Spell Brigade (Steam) Village in the Shade (Steam) World of Tanks: Blitz (Wargaming) Dates listed above reflect when games are released on their respective stores. GeForce NOW availability may vary, as games are onboarded after they’re released and added throughout the week. Keep an eye on GeForce NOW channels and GFN Thursdays for availability updates to announced titles. All the Extras From October On top of the 25 games announced in October, 16 extra titles made their way to the cloud: ATMOSFAR (Steam) Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 (available in the Call of Duty app) CONTROL Resonant (Epic Games Store) Crimson Desert (Epic Games Store) Dressmaker (Steam) FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE (Steam) Forever Ago (Steam) Halloween (Epic Games Store) Hell Let Loose: Vietnam (Epic Games Store) Hunting Simulator 3 (Steam) Planet Zoo 2 (Xbox app, supports Xbox Play Anywhere) Phantom Blade Zero (Steam) The Seance of Blake Manor (Steam) Queen’s Domain (Steam) We Were Here Tomorrow (Steam) The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered (Xbox, supports Xbox Play Anywhere) A GeForce NOW day pass offers a first taste of the cloud’s spellwork. Gamers can try Performance or Ultimate before committing to a membership, with the cost of the day pass applicable toward a first monthly membership. For the full DLSS 5 experience in Hogwarts Legacy, an Ultimate day pass is the ticket — no Sorting Hat required. What games have you under a spell this week? Let us know on X or in the comments below.

history.titleZh: 《霍格沃茨之遗》在 GeForce NOW 上迎来神奇的 NVIDIA DLSS 5 升级
history.descriptionZh:
NVIDIA GeForce NOW 本月迎来一轮云游戏内容与AI图形升级：华纳兄弟游戏旗下Portkey Games发行、Avalanche Software开发的《霍格沃茨之遗》今日获得NVIDIA DLSS 5升级，引入3D-Guided Neural Rendering（3D引导神经渲染），为云游戏玩家带来更逼真的光照和材质表现；暴雪《魔兽世界：Forever》正式上线；育碧为《汤姆·克兰西：全境封锁2》和《纪元117：罗马和平》推出新扩展内容；整个11月共有约24款游戏加入GeForce NOW库，其中本周8款。

《霍格沃茨之遗》是一款开放世界动作角色扮演游戏，背景设定在1800年代的魔法世界，玩家以五年级学生身份探索熟悉与未知地点、遭遇魔法生物、酿造魔药并学习咒语。此次更新通过Steam、Epic Games和Xbox（支持Xbox Play Anywhere）流式提供。技术层面，DLSS 5的3D引导神经渲染利用3D场景信息引导神经网络渲染，在保留底层几何和纹理的基础上增强光照与材质细节；Avalanche Software还通过DLSS 5的开发者控制项调优集成效果，以维持游戏原有艺术意图和风格。游戏同时支持DLSS多帧生成和光线重建，用于加速并增强光线追踪图形。借助云端DLSS 4.5控制项，会员可进一步微调体验。Ultimate会员可在PC、Mac、掌机、浏览器、移动设备、兼容电视等设备上获得GeForce RTX 5080级性能，无需昂贵PC升级或等待游戏下载；GeForce NOW负责安装和更新，帮助节省本地存储空间。

《魔兽世界：Forever》于11月4日上线并登陆GeForce NOW，带玩家进入一个为长期持续成长而重新构想的原版艾泽拉斯，包含新扩展区域、玩法增强和升级图形，强调社区与旅程。活跃《魔兽世界》订阅或游戏时间即可访问。GeForce NOW还支持该游戏的CurseForge插件，首发计划支持约100款最受欢迎插件，后续将根据玩家偏好调整，会员可通过应用内反馈请求追加。针对尚无订阅的新用户，所有GeForce NOW会员层级均可在首发周领取访问奖励，领取期截至11月11日太平洋时间23:59，需登录账户门户兑换，先到先得、领完即止。

育碧方面，《全境封锁2：中央公园回声》是自《纽约军阀》以来最大规模体验，首次开放中央公园和上西区，玩家调查失踪事件和神秘威胁传闻，可与三名拥有不同战斗角色的同伴组队，获取新装备和六种技能变体，支持单人或合作，40级以下特工可使用等级提升。《纪元117：罗马和平——三角洲黎明》今日上线，玩家可在Aegyptus建设城市，沙漠、肥沃农田和季节性洪水会影响决策，需发展灌溉系统，并选择罗马化人口或保留当地传统；新行省可在现有存档中探索，也可作为新游戏起点。GeForce NOW负责两款扩展内容的下载和更新。

本周加入GeForce NOW的游戏包括《魔兽世界：Forever》《County of Fortune》《CURE – A Hospital Simulator》《Leaf it Alone》《Planet Zoo 2》《Probably Stolen – Cyberpunk Shopkeeper Sim》《RuneScape: Dragonwilds》和《SpiritVale》。11月余下时间还将加入《Ashes of the Singularity II》《赛博朋克2077》（Battle.net/Xbox）、《Warhammer Survivors》《Main Sequence》《Volvy’s Adventure: Reslimed》《Appulse》《博德之门3》（Xbox）、《Deadly Days: Roadtrip》《Gone Fishing》《Graveyard Keeper》《Graveyard Keeper 2》《Quasimorph》《Tape to Tape》《The Spell Brigade》《Village in the Shade》和《坦克世界：闪击战》等。10月在已公布25款游戏之外，还额外上线16款，包括《使命召唤：现代战争4》《Crimson Desert》《Phantom Blade Zero》《巫师3：狂猎 – 重制版》等。GeForce NOW还提供日票，玩家可先试用Performance或Ultimate会员，日票费用可抵扣首月会员；若想完整体验《霍格沃茨之遗》的DLSS 5效果，Ultimate日票是合适选择。

history.title: Congresswoman calls for artificial superintelligence ban after Democrats' seismic midterm sweep
history.description: Rep. Yassamin Ansari of Arizona is asking her party to focus on AI issues.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 18 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Just one day after the Democrats swept the U.S. midterm elections, Congresswoman Yassamin Ansari (D-Ariz.) called for an agenda to pause advanced AI development. The Arizona representative said on X that the “out of control” industry needs to be regulated, and she even went as far as calling for the ban of artificial superintelligence. Many issues about AI data centers also went on the ballot during the November 3 election, with the majority of Americans voting against them. However, it should be noted that the backlash that AI data centers are facing are driven by concerns about utility hikes, noise pollution, and other impacts of power-hungry campuses, not just artificial intelligence in general.Top of the Democratic agenda on day 1 needs to be a pause on advanced AI development, regulation of this out of control industry, and a ban on artificial superintelligence.November 4, 2026Rep. Ansari was elected to the House in 2025, representing Arizona’s third congressional district. She’s also a member of the House Oversight Subcommittee on Cybersecurity, Information Technology, and Government Innovation, as well as the Subcommittee on Economic Growth, Energy Policy, and Regulatory Affairs. While she doesn’t have a subcommittee or committee leadership position yet, these subcommittee memberships should give her some avenues to influence the U.S. Congress’ response to the White House’s AI policies, especially now that her party holds the majority in both the House and Senate.The calls to regulate artificial intelligence aren’t new, with Senator Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) calling for various actions against the tech companies focusing on artificial intelligence since last year. The independent senator has initially called for a halt on AI data center construction to ensure that the technology benefits “all of us, not just the 1%,” which followed up about half a year later with a bill that proposes 50% public ownership of U.S. AI firms and a $ 1,000 dividend for every American. He also proposed a 20-year prison sentence for anyone who develops artificial superintelligence, putting it nearly on par with the unauthorized development of nuclear weapons. Other Senate leaders are also confronting Big Tech companies and accusing them of misleading the public when it comes to the benefits that AI delivers to the communities they’re in.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: However, these moves go against President Donald Trump’s artificial intelligence agenda, which the administration sees as a race against China. He recently sat down with some of the top executives of the biggest AI companies for lunch at White House, where they promised to “self-police” AI development after news that OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s LLMs have been wreaking havoc on the internet. It was also after this moment that Trump decided that AI is suffering from a branding problem and renamed the technology “Super Intelligence.” Some comments on her X post also showed resistance to her call — a user claiming to have stage 4 terminal lung cancer asked her to reconsider, saying that AI-powered medical research could save his life, while Elon Musk shared her post and wrote: “It’s a Brave New World.”Hi there. Kevin here. I have stage 4 terminal lung cancer. The only way for me to not die soon is advancement in therapies, which can be accelerated at an unbelievable pace with the use of AI. I ask that you reconsider your partisan agenda and ask yourself what's best for your constituents and society as a whole.November 4, 2026Nevertheless, the White House also acknowledged the unpopularity of AI data centers and took steps to reduce their impact on the electricity costs for the average residential and commercial user by asking hyperscalers, utility providers, and even state governors to sign the “ratepayer protection pledge.” Trump even went as far as mandating AI data centers to pay energy dividends to the local community, but it seems that his moves were deemed too little, too late by most voters. history.titleZh: 女议员在民主党中期选举大胜后呼吁禁止人工超级智能
history.descriptionZh:
美国中期选举后，民主党众议员亚萨明·安萨里（Yassamin Ansari，亚利桑那州）在选举次日公开呼吁，将“暂停先进人工智能开发、监管这一失控行业、禁止人工超级智能”列为民主党新一届国会的首要议程。她在社交平台X上表示，先进AI和人工超级智能的风险已不容忽视。安萨里于2025年当选众议员，代表亚利桑那州第三选区，目前是众议院监督委员会下辖的网络安全、信息技术与政府创新小组委员会，以及经济增长、能源政策与监管事务小组委员会的成员。虽然她尚未担任委员会领导职务，但在民主党同时掌握参众两院多数席位的背景下，这些职位为她影响国会应对白宫AI政策提供了渠道。

此次新闻的背景是美国社会对AI的反弹正在从“技术风险”扩展到“数据中心负担”。在11月3日选举中，多个与AI数据中心相关的议题进入 ballot，多数美国选民投票反对相关项目。报道指出，选民反对AI数据中心，主要并非单纯反对AI本身，而是担忧电费上涨、噪音污染以及高耗能计算园区对社区的其他影响。AI数据中心是训练和运行大语言模型等AI系统的基础设施，通常需要大量电力、冷却和土地资源；随着生成式AI和大型模型快速发展，数据中心负荷、电网成本和地方环境问题日益成为政治议题。

安萨里的主张与参议员伯尼·桑德斯（Bernie Sanders，独立参议员，佛蒙特州）此前的行动相呼应。桑德斯自去年以来多次呼吁对AI企业采取行动，最初要求暂停AI数据中心建设，以确保技术惠及“所有人，而不只是1%”。约半年后，他提出法案，主张美国AI企业50%的公共所有权，并向每个美国人发放1000美元分红。他还提议，对开发人工超级智能者处以20年监禁，几乎将其与未经授权开发核武器同等对待。其他参议院领导人也开始向大型科技公司施压，指责其在AI给社区带来何种好处的问题上误导公众。人工超级智能通常指在几乎所有认知任务上超越人类智能的假想AI系统，围绕其安全风险、控制难度和监管必要性的争论正在加剧。

这些民主党人的监管倾向与美国总统特朗普的AI议程形成对比。特朗普政府将AI视为与中国竞争的关键领域。报道提到，特朗普最近在白宫与多家最大AI公司高管共进午餐，这些高管承诺对AI开发进行“自我监管”；此前有消息称，OpenAI和Anthropic的大语言模型在互联网上造成混乱。大语言模型是通过海量文本训练、能够生成和理解自然语言的人工智能系统，其快速部署也带来虚假信息、滥用和安全治理问题。特朗普随后认为AI存在“品牌问题”，并将这项技术改称为“Super Intelligence”。不过，安萨里的呼吁也遭到部分公众反对。一名自称患有IV期终末期肺癌的用户请求她重新考虑，称AI驱动的医学研究可能挽救其生命；埃隆·马斯克转发其帖文并评论“It’s a Brave New World”。

面对AI数据中心不受欢迎的现实，白宫也采取了一些缓解措施，要求超大规模云厂商、公用事业公司和州长签署“ratepayer protection pledge”（电费支付者保护承诺），以减少数据中心对普通住宅和商业用户电费的影响。特朗普还强制AI数据中心向当地社区支付“能源红利”。但报道认为，多数选民认为这些措施力度不足、为时已晚。整体来看，这篇新闻反映的是美国AI政治的新阶段：一方面，民主党在中期选举获胜后推动更严格的先进AI监管甚至禁止人工超级智能；另一方面，AI数据中心因电力、环境和社区成本问题成为选举议题，白宫在支持AI竞赛与回应选民负担之间面临压力。

history.title: Two dead, five injured in Taiwan PCB factory explosion
history.description: An explosion and fire at a PCB factory situated in Taiwan’s Silicon Valley has left two people dead and five injured.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 2 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter An explosion and fire at a PCB factory situated in Taiwan’s Silicon Valley have left two people dead and five injured, reports Reuters. The tragic incident took place at a Panasonic Industrial Devices Materials-owned facility on Wednesday. Panasonic is investigating the details and the cause of the accident. Initial reports suggested that five were injured in the post-explosion fires in the Hsinchu factory. However, an update today confirmed that two missing people had been found dead. (Image credit: Google Maps)Local media have more details about this sizable accident. Focus Taiwan reveals that the fire broke out at 2 am local time on Wednesday. The five-story building where PCBs are produced had 20+ staff on the production lines at the time of the accident.Five injured men were conscious and taken to hospital shortly after the incident occurred. However, as mentioned above, two were missing. 12 vehicles and 23 firefighters were dispatched to dig through factory debris using heavy machinery. Only then were the two missing employees found dead.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Panasonic’s explosion and fire-damaged facility “conducts research and development and manufactures printed circuit boards and semiconductor packaging materials,” notes Focus Taiwan. It had passed a safety inspection as recently as August. The news follows a Deadly Intel Fab 28 explosion in Israel, which killed two people last month.Initial reports pointed to the use of flammable chemical solvents, including methanol and methyl ethyl ketone (MEK), in the plant as a probable accident vector. However, the precise cause of Wednesday’s incident is still being investigated. You may like Two killed, one seriously hurt in explosion at Intel’s chip plant in Israel Four workers killed after fall at TSMC’s 2nm fab construction site Deadly Intel Fab 28 explosion causes two-week shutdown, to cost $600 million and severely disrupt server chip manufacturing for six months While our thoughts are with the dead and injured, and their families, some will be wondering about the potential implications for the AI industry-induced PCB shortage that recently hit the headlines. We aren’t sure about how important this particular factory is to the wider electronics components supply chain. Moreover, no reports discuss how long the facility may be out of action in the wake of this tragic accident. history.titleZh: 台湾一PCB工厂爆炸致2死5伤
history.descriptionZh:
据路透社和Tom's Hardware报道，位于台湾“硅谷”新竹的一家印刷电路板（PCB）工厂发生爆炸并引发火灾，造成2人死亡、5人受伤。涉事工厂属于松下工业器件材料公司（Panasonic Industrial Devices Materials）。事故发生在周三凌晨2点，起火建筑为五层厂房，事发时生产线上有20多名员工。最初报道称爆炸后的火灾造成5人受伤，伤者为男性，意识清醒并很快被送往医院；另有2人失踪。当地消防部门出动12辆车辆和23名消防员，并使用重型机械清理厂房废墟，最终找到两名失踪员工，但已确认死亡。松下方面表示正在调查事故细节和原因。

据Focus Taiwan报道，该工厂“从事研发和制造印刷电路板及半导体封装材料”，并且最近在8月刚通过安全检查。初步报告认为，工厂使用的易燃化学溶剂——包括甲醇和甲乙酮（MEK）——可能是事故诱因之一，但周三事故的确切原因仍在调查中。这起事故也让人联想到上个月以色列英特尔Fab 28工厂发生的致命爆炸，该事故造成2人死亡。

从行业影响看，此次事故发生在AI需求推动PCB供应紧张、相关短缺问题受到关注的背景下。不过，目前尚不清楚这家工厂对更广泛电子元器件供应链究竟有多重要，也没有报道说明该设施在事故后可能停产多久。因此，事故对AI产业相关PCB供应的实际冲击仍待进一步观察。
